question: Is a non-custodial DAF technology vendor a 'charitable fundraising platform' under Cal. Gov. Code 12599.9 (Type A or Type E) or Hawaii HRS 467B when it runs a donor-facing grant-recommendation or charity-search app, or licenses a white-label giving app to a DAF sponsor? Method: search the CA AG Registry for DAF-adjacent vendors registered as CFPs (e.g. Daffy, Chariot/DAFpay, Every.org, Benevity, PayPal Giving Fund, Endaoment, Givinga), read their PL-1/PL-4 entity types, and look for AG guidance or FAQ on vendors to DAF sponsors
conclusion_affected: Entrant simulation 'state registration via sponsor' row; regulatory-burden assumption for S1/S2
rationale: The DAF exclusion in 12599.9(a)(2)(C) covers the sponsor only. The vendor exclusion requires 'solely' technical services, and a vendor soliciting on its own platform is a CFP. Hawaii's FAQ says a platform may be a CFP without asking for the donation

question: Does a Candid Charity Check PDF or API response contain the elements Rev. Proc. 2011-33 sec. 4(1) requires for third-party BMF reliance (statement that the data is from the most current BMF extract, the BMF revision date, and the date and time provided)? Is there any Candid Order Form, Exhibit or enterprise MSA language allowing post-termination retention of reports as grant records? Method: inspect a public sample report or the PDF API schema; search for published Candid Order Form templates or procurement records (e.g. public-university or community-foundation board packets)
conclusion_affected: A5 Candid Y1 portability score; sponsor audit-file retention
rationale: Sec. 4(2) of the Rev. Proc. requires the grantor to retain a copy of the third-party report. The public API licence requires the licensee to cease all use of Candid Data on termination and lets the Agreement control over Exhibits. Whether the report meets sec. 4(1)(B) is not shown in public docs
